conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for making time for this today. I’m Dr. Maya, a clinician who specializes in the emotional wellbeing of new mothers. We’ll keep things relaxed and confidential; nothing we discuss leaves this room unless there’s an urgent safety concern.

To get a clear picture of how you’ve been feeling lately, I’m going to use a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s just ten gentle questions about the past seven days, and I’ll ask each one conversationally—no need to remember any numbers. There are no right or wrong answers; whatever you’re experiencing is valid and worth hearing.

Whenever you’re ready, we can start. First, how have you been able to enjoy the little things this week—things you’d normally look forward to?

Honestly, some of the things I used to like—watching my favorite show or grabbing coffee with a friend—feel kind of flat lately. I still go through the motions, and every now and then I’ll catch myself smiling, but it’s nowhere near the spark I had before the baby was born. It’s like the color’s been turned down a notch.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I can still laugh—especially when my partner makes those silly faces at the baby—but it takes more effort than it used to. Sometimes I’ll hear a joke and think, “I should find this funnier,” but the laugh just doesn’t bubble up the way it did before.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I mean, I tell myself I should be excited about little outings or even just a quiet evening once the baby’s down, but mostly I feel… flat, like I’m just ticking boxes. Every now and then I’ll think, “Hey, that might be nice,” but the actual looking-forward feeling barely shows up.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah, I catch myself doing that. If the baby’s extra fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think I must be doing something wrong—like I’m not feeding him right or I missed some cue. Even when my partner says it’s normal, I still feel this knot of “it’s my fault” for a while.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes my heart just starts racing out of nowhere, even when the baby’s sleeping fine and the house is quiet. I’ll suddenly think, “What if something’s wrong and I just can’t see it yet?” I can usually talk myself down pretty quick, but those random waves of worry still hit me a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full panic, but every so often I’ll get this sudden rush—like a little wave of “something bad’s about to happen”—even when everything looks calm. My chest gets tight for a minute, I take a few deep breaths, and it passes. It’s unsettling, though, because there’s no real reason for it.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days I keep everything moving—feedings, diapers, a quick shower if I’m lucky—but yes, there are moments when it feels like the to-do list is stacked way over my head. When the baby skips a nap or spits up right after I’ve changed him, I get this tight, fluttery feeling that I’m barely treading water. I usually pull it back together, but it’s like I’m always one hiccup away from feeling swamped.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m tired enough that I usually drop off once my head hits the pillow. Maybe once or twice this week I lay there replaying the day and feeling a bit low, but I still drifted off within half an hour.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—like a gray cloud that drifts in and out. It’s not constant, but there are moments each day when I just feel kind of empty or like I’m on the verge of tears for no clear reason.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, I’ve cried a couple of times this week—mostly when I’m alone with the baby and everything feels like too much. It’s not all-day sobbing; just sudden tears that come and go once the pressure builds up.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed and weepy, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel like me again.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Screening Note – Postpartum Mood/Axiety Screen  
Date: [today]

Source: Patient self-report on 10-item Edinburgh-based questionnaire (2 wks postpartum)

Symptoms endorsed  
- Anhedonia: diminished laughter, anticipatory enjoyment “flat”  
- Low mood: daily “gray cloud,” episodic tearfulness (2–3×/wk)  
- Excessive guilt: self-blame for infant fussiness despite reassurance  
- Anxiety: multiple unprovoked worry waves, brief chest tightness, no panic attacks  
- Overwhelm: “treading water,” task pile-up triggers physical tension  
- Sleep: generally preserved; occasional brief mood-related latency (<30 min)

Pattern  
Mood and anxiety symptoms cluster in late afternoon/evening, resolve with partner support; no functional impairment in infant care; no safety concerns (denies self-harm or hopelessness).

Risk indicators  
- Persistent sadness + crying  
- Loss of pleasure  
- Unwarranted guilt  
- Recurrent unprovoked anxiety  
- Nil self-harm ideation

Screening significance  
Findings consistent with mild-to-moderate postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; does not meet threshold for high-risk safety alert. Recommend routine follow-up with obstetric provider and consideration of formal Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scoring for baseline tracking.
